SFT -> RL. In our fine-tuning notebooks, we typically say that rollouts that go past the max context length (too much reasoning) get 0 reward, so there is slight pressure for shorter reasoning, but I don't think we have strong regularization. I think the agreed-upon recipe is to first make the model smarter (longer reasoning), then teach it to reason faster/denser.

Which specific model? and are tools available? I would say that there is lots of RL with tool use, but that the reasoning traces are not always perfect. In general, models think about things that might be wrong, but will recover from this poor line of thinking.

children.author: CMay
samstevens
children.text: Can you describe more in terms of what moderation you want? I can say with confidence that we don't train for the typical adult-only content you can see on some "de-safe'd" models, but it's not clear to me exactly what you're asking about. We can also discuss over email if you prefer.

Did y'all do any particular work that makes these models great for moderation? One of the issues between cloud models vs local is that often people are trying to push the limit of what their hardware can do and it doesn't leave too much headroom for moderation to make the models a little more constrained for kids or schools to use locally, or just for family in general who don't want accidental unhinged results.

In the past I've noticed that some LFM were way better at moderation than much larger models. Not necessarily prejudging what is acceptable, but allowing you to interrogate content with a series of questions to customize the moderation. Other models I tested were far worse.

Decision models are like the next optimization in that direction, but none of the benchmarks for the popular models ever show how good they are at tasks like content moderation. The smaller and more efficient we can get that workload, the more that it can simply be on by default in a lot of use cases without feeling like you're giving up a lot of performance, creative freedom or accuracy. You can't have a high number of false positives or people would rather take control back.

We need local content moderation to be cool, efficient, accurate and configurable so that people can get the higher quality results which unsafe models tend to produce, while filtering out the unsafe results fast enough that it can even be done in an agentic way and fed back into the model to steer its results.

children.text: I initially tried annotating everything three times, then judging the annotation with the same model. That failed predictably, so yeah just logprobs right now, judged on a hand-annotated dataset. Mostly correlated - ~80%.

One thing I have been using LFM 2.6 for is annotating emails, text messages, and other metadata. I keep it all ingesting into one giant database and annotate it all as it comes in on an RTX A4500. The LFM annotations are basically triage, and then slowly annotations trickle into my halo model based on lowest confidence (right now that's DeepSeek 4.1 Flash 1017) for an upgraded annotation. (Agents can then search this database for context).

Excited to roll out LFM 3 to replace it, looks like a big step up. Right now LFM 2.6 gets trustworthy annotations on just over 40% of data points. Just waiting for these to get into LocalAI.
